meta.title: Signs of Winter — Set 5
meta.subject: English Reading
meta.description: Challenge quiz testing inference, cause-and-effect, and comparisons in 'Signs of Winter'.

questions.question: What is the main message (theme) of 'Signs of Winter'?
options: Winter brings changes in weather, plants, and animals, and living things prepare to survive it
France is the coldest place in the world during December
Beavers are the only animals that store food in the autumn
Snowmen are very easy to build for young children
questions.explanation: The text shows how the winter season affects weather and how plants and animals adapt to survive the cold.

questions.question: We can infer that winter temperatures are much lower than autumn temperatures.
questions.explanation: True. Winter comes after autumn, and the temperature gets colder, causing rain to turn to snow.

questions.question: Why do some animals move to warmer places for the winter?
options: Because the cold temperature makes it hard to find food and stay warm
To help beavers build their wooden lodges
To find pine needles to eat in the mountains
To learn how to go sledding down hills
questions.explanation: Some animals migrate (move) because they cannot survive the freezing cold or find food when the ground is snow-covered.

questions.question: American bisons migrate to warmer countries to escape the winter cold.
questions.explanation: False. Bisons do not move away; instead, they stay and grow extra long, thick coats of fur to keep warm.

questions.question: Why does the text include 'Did You Know?' boxes?
options: To share interesting extra facts about winter, countries, and animals
To list new vocabulary spelling words
To show readers how to roll a huge snowball
To explain why winter is better than spring
questions.explanation: 'Did You Know?' boxes are text features that provide interesting, extra information related to the main topic.

questions.question: We can infer that deciduous trees lose their leaves to save energy when temperatures are _______ in winter.
questions.explanation: Deciduous trees shed leaves to conserve water and energy when the temperature is cold and sunlight is scarce.

questions.question: Based on the text, why is it winter in New Zealand in July while it is winter in France in December?
options: Because they are on opposite sides of Earth, which tilt closer or farther from the sun at different times
Because New Zealand is always much closer to the North Pole than France
Because beavers only collect logs in New Zealand in July
Because the sun goes to sleep in July in the Southern Hemisphere
questions.explanation: Seasons are opposite in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres because different parts of Earth get farther or closer to the sun as Earth travels.

questions.question: Sort the survival methods of animals in winter based on whether they Prepare Food or Change Body/Fur:
questions.explanation: Collecting logs/bark and storing nuts are food preparations. Growing long coats and warm fur are physical changes.

questions.question: Building a snowman and riding down hills on a sled are both fun outdoor winter activities for humans.
questions.explanation: True. The text mentions children building snowmen and Bobby going sledding as examples of winter recreation.

questions.question: Arrange the words to explain how animals handle the winter:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Animals adapt to survive winter.' Adaptations include thick fur and food storage.

questions.question: What causes it to snow instead of rain in the winter?
options: The air temperature becomes very cold
Clouds disappear from the sky
Earth travels too close to the sun
Evergreen trees lose their pine needles
questions.explanation: When the temperature drops below freezing, water vapor in clouds freezes and falls as snow instead of rain.

questions.question: Because there is very little daylight in winter, the days are much _______ than in summer.
questions.explanation: Daylight is short in winter, making the day length much shorter than the long days of summer.

questions.question: Arrange the words to show what changes the seasons:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'The sun changes the seasons.' Earth's position relative to the sun creates the seasons.

questions.question: We can infer that evergreen trees are better adapted to cold, dry winter winds than deciduous trees that lose their leaves.
questions.explanation: True. Evergreen needles are thick and waxy, helping them retain water and stay on the trees all winter.

questions.question: What is the correct cause-and-effect chain for winter seasonal change?
options: Earth travels around sun -> parts move farthest from sun -> temperature gets cold -> it snows and trees lose leaves
Beavers collect logs -> lodges are built in water -> Bobby goes sledding -> sun travels around Earth
Bisons grow thick coats -> temperature drops -> pine needles stay green -> children make a huge snowball
Winter comes after autumn -> daylight gets longer -> New Zealand gets warmer -> clouds disappear
questions.explanation: The movement of Earth around the sun causes parts to get farther away, resulting in colder temperatures, snow, and leafless trees.
